metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward; delay or dampen the correction to allow for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.5) over 3–5 days, model underestimates downward trend; increase forecast bias downward by 1–2% to align with sentiment.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early part of 30-day horizon (days 1–5) when sentiment is volatile; apply slight upward bias to first 3–5 days.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40) and sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to reflect stronger downward bias.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags in adjusting; apply early correction to reflect sentiment shift, especially if recent sentiment >0.5.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate true price in the last 5–7 days when sentiment is positive; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to final 5–7 days.
